Heard was eventually granted a restraining order, but Depp denied the allegations. An LAPD spokesman later toldPeoplethat following their investigation, there was "no evidence of any crime." The contentious he said, she said was the first in a slew of headline-making court cases between the exes. Most notably, Heard wrote an op-ed forThe Washington Postin 2018, claiming, "I spoke up against sexual violence — and faced our culture's wrath." She didn't mention Depp by name, but even so, he filed a defamation suit against her in 2019. Along the course of the trial, Depp seemed to not take it very seriously. While Heard made allegations that her ex physically and sexually assaulted her, the actor denied her claims and kept busy doodling and drawing viral sketches with colored markers. He eventually won the lawsuit in 2022 and was awarded $10.4 million in damages. In 2008, it seemed like Chris Brown and Rihanna were hip hop's It couple. The pair met as teenagers at the Vibe Awards, and over the next few years, they grew from collaborators to best friends to totally in love. Unfortunately, not all was as rosy as it seemed from the red carpet. In 2009,TMZreleased disturbing photographs of Rihanna, who was reportedly beaten by Brown after a pre-Grammy party. Not long after this, the full police report surfaced online, and Brown pleaded guilty to felony assault. He was sentenced to five years probation and six months community labor, reportedBillboard. Brown later admitted in the documentary "Chris Brown: Welcome to My Life" (viaPeople) that he "felt like a f***ing monster" after the incident with Rihanna. He eventually did find love with model Karrueche Tran. Unfortunately, old patterns appeared to resurface. According toE! News, Tran alleged Brown punched her in the stomach, pushed her down the stairs, and threatened to shoot and kill her on numerous occasions. Tran was granted a permanent restraining order after sharing angry texts in which Brown threatened to "beat the s***" out of her. Mariah Carey has certainly been through the ringer when it comes to love. Her early marriage to her label boss Tommy Mottola was allegedly so abusive that she had to get permission to leave the house. She also endured a traumatic child abuse investigation (she and then-husband Nick Cannon came out in the clear) and a highly publicized mental breakdown. Through it all, Cannon seemed to be a solid support for the troubled singer. It was only after the pair divorced that Carey allegedly started treating her romantic partners like garbage, and it was fiancé James Packer who supposedly bore the brunt of that bad juju. According toDaily Mail, Carey allegedly threw Packer's laptop out a window in 2016 because he played a Beyoncé song. The pair split before tying the knot, with Carey's team claiming she wasn't happy with his behavior. Packer's rep fired back, tellingPeople,"[T]ypical Mariah to just twist things that don't sound good to her. They split because she has issues." The following year, one of Carey's former security guards threatened to sue the songstress for sexual harassment. According toTMZ, he claimed she exposed herself to him and intentionally performed sexual acts while he was in view. Carey came clean about her struggle with bipolar disorder in early 2018, so perhaps she has changed for the better after seeking treatment. Brad Pitt has certainly had some tumultuous relationships, and if you asked his ex-wives, he seems to be the common denominator. In the early '00s, Pitt's divorce from Jennifer Aniston prompted the press to essentially frame the actress as the world's saddest lady for the rest of her career. What happened? Pitt supposedly had an emotional affair with co-star Angelina Jolie on the set of "Mr. and Mrs. Smith." The new lovers claimed they took things to the next level only after his split with Aniston, though Pitt later said the aforementioned movie is his favorite because, as he toldRolling Stone, it's where he "fell in love." And get this: Before Pitt's divorce from Aniston was finalized, he posed for an epicW magazinephoto shoot with Jolie. The piece, titled "Domestic Bliss," cast the two "friends" as a sexy husband and wife with kids. In response, Aniston toldVanity Fairthat Pitt has "a sensitivity chip that's missing." As for Brangelina, they appeared to have it good for nearly a decade, but in 2016, they went through an explosive breakup and nasty custody battle. Pitt toldGQthat substance abuse was at the root of his relationship's "self-inflicted" collapse. "I can't remember a day since I got out of college when I wasn't boozing or had a spliff, or something," he said. Though that all sounds awful trashy, Pitt has since reportedly embarked on a cleaner lifestyle. It seems like mixing business with pleasure is a recipe for disaster — at least for Calvin Harris' girlfriends. The Scottish DJ has a terrible track record when it comes to working with his significant others. His 2014 split with pop star Rita Ora seemed amicable until Harris allegedly blindsided her by publicly announcing their breakup on Twitter (viaBillboard) months after the fact — weird, but okay. Things got worse from there. Ora was scheduled to perform her hit "I Will Never Let You Down" at the 2014 Teen Choice Awards, but Harris reportedly wouldn't give her legal permission to do so. Ora had to cancel the performance because Harris owned the copyright. If Harris' experience with Ora didn't reach peak-level petty, the demise of his relationship with Taylor Swift certainly did. The drama unfolded when fans discovered Swift helped write Harris' Rihanna collaboration, "This Is What You Came For." Swift used the pseudonym "Nils Sjoberg" to reportedly avoid overshadowing anyone on the track (girl gets a lot of attention). After its release, Harris claimed he "couldn't see" himself working with Swift — something Swift's camp apparently took as a mega-burn and whad'ya know, word soon got out that Swift helped Harris write the track. Harris eventually came clean, but in the same breath, he also accused his ex of trying to make him look bad in a Twitter tantrum (viaUs Weekly). As ill-fated as that tweetstorm was, Harris did eventually apologize. Back in 2018, Jalena was still an inescapable force. The notorious relationship began in 2010 when Selena Gomez and Justin Bieber were innocent teens on an innocent date at IHOP. Oh, how things went so wrong in a few long years (it felt like a lifetime, did it not?). Bieber was reportedly not the best boyfriend to sweet Gomez. After all, he allegedly penned the track "Sorry" about the "Good for You" songstress. What does he have to be sorry for? A whole lot. Some highlights include the time he got into a fist fight with Orlando Bloom after allegedly hooking up with Bloom's ex-wife. This move seemed purely spiteful because Gomez was rumored to be canoodling with Bloom at the time. While Gomez was struggling with Lupus, Biebs was busy getting arrested for drunk driving and resisting arrest, egging his neighbor's home, and urinating in a custodian's mop bucket. Classy. Though they had both dated other people when apart, these two kept winding up together. In 2018, after reportedly reuniting for the umpteenth time, Gomez's mom, Mandy Teefey, admitted in an interview with Gossip Cop that she was "not happy" about the rumored return of the Biebs (viaTeen Vogue). Adam Levine may have a voice that's sweet as sugar, but the way he's acted in past relationships is anything but. Lavine allegedly dumped his supermodel girlfriend Nina Agdal by completely ghosting her. According toUs Weekly,he stopped answering her calls, then eventually informed her of his engagement to on-and-off flame and fellow model Behati Prinsloo through a text message. Levine certainly has a way with words in his songs, but when it comes to real-life communication, that's apparently not the case. He allegedly also dumped Jessica Simpson via text message. He embarrassed cocktail waitress Rebecca Ginos by telling Howard Stern (viaE! News) they had sex on the first day they met, and he shamed actress Lindsay Lohan by simultaneously saying that he never slept with her and that she probably slept with a lot of people. Oh, and he reportedly mortified Victoria's Secret model Anne Vyalitsyna by telling the world they used the "pull-out method" (viaThe Daily Beast). It seems Levine has never been one for relationship tact, though he did allegedly reach out to his exes to apologize before marrying Prinsloo in the summer of 2014. Most of us remember Tom Cruise's relationships by their fairy-tale moments, like his famous movies alongside Nicole Kidman, or that time he jumped on Oprah's couch to exuberantly proclaim his love for Katie Holmes. What we don't remember are how those love stories played out. Amid his growing dedication to Scientology in 2001, Cruise abruptly filed for divorce from Kidman after 10 years of marriage. Though Kidman admitted to DuJour Magazine (viaPeople) that it was a "shock to [her] system," she did quip to David Letterman (viaThe Standard), "At least I can wear heels now." In no world is stealthily exiting a decade-long marriage like it's "Mission: Impossible" commendable behavior, but apparently, Cruise did it anyway. His relationship with Katie Holmes, which was long rumored to be a contract marriage, may have been even more out of control. According toMirror,Holmes had to follow a long list of bizarre marriage rules, including complete silence during labor. She allegedly wasn't allowed to utter a single peep while delivering Suri, and according to some reports, she feared for her safety after filing for divorce because of the church. Of course, this is speculation at its finest, but it's certainly the kind of trash talking that would make us wary of another Cruise wedding. Gwyneth Paltrow has painted herself a well-intentioned (albeit sometimes clueless) wealthy single mama. She spends her days promoting bizarre vaginal steam spas and $1,220 casserole dishes. Nothing about her carefully crafted image would lead us to believe she's a terrible romantic partner, but the actress has admitted she has her flaws. "I'm actually a pretty good friend, and a good sister and daughter and mother, but I'm at my potentially most vulnerable and f***ed up in the romantic slice of the pie," she told "Girlboss Radio" (viaE! News). Paltrow does at least make an effort to "consciously uncouple" rather than ghosting her flames, and that's probably why she remains in good standing with most of her exes. However, that doesn't mean dating the Oscar-winning actress is all roses. According toE! News, cheating rumors emerged when Paltrow was spotted kissing her ex, Donovan Leitch, at a Dodgers game just six days after announcing her split from Coldplay frontman Chris Martin. In the past, Paltrow has admitted that her relationships rarely make it past six weeks and that — as she told Diane Sawyer (viaABC News) — she's sometimes the "architect of [her] own misery." Well, at least she's honest. Kardashians generally take the moral high road when it comes to relationships — from Khloé Kardashian supporting her troubled ex-husband during his recovery to Kris Jenner supporting her ex-husband's transition into womanhood long after their divorce. Rob Kardashian is the exception to the rule. Rob's relationship with Blac Chyna seemed insanely tumultuous by tabloid accounts. These included the explosive fights documented throughout their reality TV show, "Rob & Chyna," abuse claims and restraining orders, and their apparent affinity for airing their grievances on social media. In 2017, after an exhausting year and a half of on-and-off dating, Chyna took to Snapchat (viaUs Weekly) to claim Rob beat her up. She also allegedly sent Rob a video of herself kissing another man in an effort to get him to leave her alone. Rob countered by posting several explicit photos of her online in what appeared to be some sort ofderanged (and potentially criminal) hours-long social media rant. This incident was the final straw for Chyna, who filed a restraining order. Her lawyer, Lisa Bloom, had this to say in a statement (viaCNN): "Mr. Kardashian, you are now on notice: revenge porn is illegal. Cyberbullying your ex is harassment. ... Your attempts to shame and control [Chyna] are hereby rejected." Actress Emma Roberts may look like an innocent girl next door, but that doesn't mean she isn't vicious when it comes to matters of the heart. Rumor has it the actress physically abused her boyfriend, actor Evan Peters. The couple reportedly met while filming "Adult World" and were later cast together in "American Horror Story."For the first year or so of their relationship, they were the poster children for millennial power couples. Then came 2013, when Roberts was arrested for allegedly assaulting Peters in Canada, asTMZreported. Though Peters reportedly suffered a bloody nose and bite marks, he didn't press charges, and Roberts was released. According to a totally real and not at all made up source that spoke toOK!magazine, Roberts has also brought her problematic relationship issues to set. "Basically, as soon as the director yells, 'Cut,' Emma and Evan are making out. That is, if they're not screaming at each other," said the anonymous insider. The two later got engaged but called it quits in 2019, putting their trashy moments together behind them for good. You don't have to watch "Jersey Shore" for long to realize Ronnie Ortiz-Magro doesn't have much tact when it comes to relationships. Audiences may recall the anonymous note some housemates typed to warn Sammi "Sweetheart" Giancola about her man's trifling ways. The infamous note (viaMTV) said that when Giancola wasn't around, Ortiz-Magro "put his head between a cocktail waitress' breasts," made out with two girls, and "was grinding with multiple fat women." Believe it or not: Those weren't his worst offenses. AsLife & Stylereported, the star's relationship with Giancola was the most toxic on the show. How could it not be when it was clouded with a heavy stream of "Ron Ron Juice" and fights that escalated to the point where he actually tried to throw Giancola and her entire bed onto the porch? If you think Giancola had it bad, you haven't yet seen "Jersey Shore: Family Vacation." After Ortiz-Magro settled into the Miami house, it didn't take long for him to completely forget about his pregnant girlfriend Jen Harley. He invited a group of girls back to use the hot tub and did something suspicious behind a closed bathroom door. Later that year, Ortiz-Magro appeared to have a physical fight with Harley on Instagram Live. We should mention that Harley was arrested for domestic battery after allegedly dragging her baby's daddy with a car, asUs Weeklyreported, so let's give thanks these two have since called it quits. Every reality show needs a villain. For "Vanderpump Rules,"Jax Taylor is the guy for the job. Sure, Taylor has done some pretty noble things in his time on the Bravo series. He paid for girlfriend Brittany Cartwright's breast implants and even convinced her to go bigger than planned. "I'm ready to throw some Ds on this," he told doctors (viaDaily Mail). "Go big or go home." What a sweetheart, right? Wrong. Fans who've been with the series since the start remember when the reality stud cheated on Stassi Schroeder with her best friend, Kristen Doute. Years later, Schroeder introduced him on her podcast "Straight Up With Stassi" (viaBravo) as a guy who did "bad things on the reg." Taylor has been surprisingly open about his flaws (at least the ones he's self-aware enough to recognize). He admitted to Schroeder that he "didn't think" before cheating. "I just did it, and I didn't care." Cartwright and Taylor became an item after meeting in Vegas in 2015. Though she claimed to Bravo'sThe Daily Dishthat he fell in love with her "at first sight," he's got a funny way of showing it. According toBustle,he floated a salacious rumor that he walked in on Cartwright having sex with Doute, but in reality, he was the one sneaking around. In Season 6, we learned that Taylor slept with ex-SURver Faith Stowers and had been trashing Cartwright, asUs Weeklyreported. He has since sought reiki healing. There's a reason Jesse James is a notorious Hollywood bad boy. The guy has a terrible track record with women. Beloved Oscar-winning actress Sandra Bullock famously divorced the "Monster Garage" star after he was caught cheating on her with the kind of gal who'd allegedly tattoo a swastika on her stomach. Not only did he mess with Miss Congeniality, but he also toldDaily Mailthat cheating is a "part of life" and "a lot of good" came from the dissolution of his marriage. Nice, right? Mistreating America's sweetheart wasn't an isolated incident. According toPeople,he announced his engagement to tattoo artist Kat Von D less than a year after divorcing Bullock, telling Howard Stern (viaUs Weekly) that she was better in bed.Six months later, Von D called off the wedding, claiming in a lengthyFacebook postthat James cheated on her with 19 different women. Shocking, right? James them moved on to wife No. 4, billionaire heiress Alexis DeJoria, who had been subject to the same cheating scandals as the women before her. In an interview withInTouch,hair stylist Myla Harris claimed she exchanged racy social media messages with James during his relationship with DeJoria. Was this — or the fact that by 2020, DeJoria and James had decided to divorce — really news? Kristen Stewart may not have treated all her partners like trash, but she certainly did a doozy on Robert Pattinson. The "Twilight" lovers had the kind of glittering romance that Hollywood dies for (figuratively, of course, considering vampires live forever). Less than four months before the premiere of "Twilight's" final installment, Stewart found herself embroiled in one of young Hollywood's most shocking cheating scandals. According toUs Weekly,she became romantically involved with director Rupert Sanders while filming "Snow White and the Huntsman."When photos emerged of the pair making out, "Twilight" fans were stunned. Sanders had a wife and children, by the way. "I lit my universe on fire and I watched it burn," the actress told Marie Claire (viaDaily Mail) at the time. "Speaking very candidly, it was a really traumatic period in my early 20s that kick-started something in me that was a bit more feral." So there you have it. She's more werewolf than vampire, after all. When you catch your British hunk cheating with the nanny, it's time to get yourself a James Bond-worthy love triangle — at least if you're going by the Sienna Miller playbook. According toReuters, when a tabloid journalist pulled a 007 and hacked into actor Daniel Craig's cellphone, the spy found an incriminating voicemail of Miller saying "I love you" to the James Bond star. She was still with the philandering Jude Law at the time. During the News Corp. phone hacking trial, Miller addressed the incident to London's Old Bailey Court (viaReuters), reportedly describing Craig as her best friend. "Whether or not I was in a relationship with Daniel Craig at the time, it was a very brief encounter," she said. Law also owned up to grilling Craig about the alleged affair during the trial. The starlet has admitted to doing "immoral" things. "When I wasn't at work, I wasn't behaving the way you should," she told Esquire (viaUs Weekly). Perhaps she was referring to the whatever-it-was with Craig, or maybe she was alluding to her affair with actor Balthazar Getty, who was married with four children when he ran off with Miller. "I probably seem like not a particularly nice person, not a girl's girl," she told GQ (viaUs Weekly). Model Christie Brinkley and architect Peter Cook had a notoriously nasty divorce battle. In an interview with Matt Lauer (viaUs Weekly), Brinkley claimed her husband was purposely making her miserable. "I just want peace. And every time I have any joy or any kind of success in anything, he has to try to destroy it," she said. Here's the thing: Peter Cook didn't just cheat on Brinkley — he reportedly cheated on her with a teenager he hired as an assistant. According to "Today"(viaPeople) Cook met Diana Bianchi when she was 18 years old. Their trysts occurred at the office and in Brinkley's homes in The Hamptons. During their divorce trial (viaThe Sydney Morning Herald), Bianchi testified that Cook "hid cash for her under a rock and gave her $15,000 to help her buy a Nissan Maxima." When the affair ended, he reportedly sent Bianchi a $300,000 payout because he was concerned about her filing a sexual harassment lawsuit. According toPage Six,Cook's divorce from Suzanne Shaw was equally ugly. She claimed in an email that he had a "pathological" desire for young women and filmed himself with a prostitute.Page Sixalso reported that he was spotted taking "creepy" photos of girls without their knowledge and snuggling up to a 21-year-old student. Eminem may be a rap icon, but the star rose to fame off the back of controversial lyrics that depicted extreme violence against women. Some of his songs targeted his ex-wife Kim Mathers, the mother of his child. A track titled "Kim" depicts a disturbing fantasy about a murder-suicide. It was so vulgar it was left off the clean version of "The Marshall Mathers LP." In an interview with Dr. Keith Ablow (viaPeople),Kim claimed Eminem's abuse led her to attempt suicide. Things reportedly came to a head when she saw her on-and-off husband beating up a blow-up doll that looked like her onstage. "When Marshall's first tour started is when his ego just went 'poof,'" she told Ablow. "Like he was God, that's what he thought. ... I was just told that I should be grateful that he still talks to me." In 2017, Eminem released the track "Bad Husband," in which he apologizes to his ex-wife. Wilmer Valderrama — yes, the dude who played Fez on "That '70s Show" — is one of Hollywood's most covert playboys. His dating history reads like a who's who of early '00s teen stars. ThoughUs Weeklyreported that the actor remained a rock for long-term girlfriend Demi Lovato after their relationship ended, he wasn't always such a loyal guy. The actor revealed some not-so-nice things during a salacious interview with Howard Stern. According toThe Daily Beast,he gave actress Jennifer Love Hewitt a sex rating of eight; called singer Ashlee Simpson "a screamer," and commented on actress Lindsay Lohan's waxing habits. The class act also allegedly lied about taking Mandy Moore's virginity, claiming, "The sex with Mandy was good, but it wasn't like warm apple pie." Moore toldEllethat Valderrama's story was "utterly tacky," untrue, and hurtful. If you date this guy, you may want to make him sign a nondisclosure agreement. Kris Jenner is running an empire, but somehow, she still had time for the odd affair. There have long been rumors that the Kardashian matriarch bedded O.J. Simpson — and that the football star is Khloé Kardashian's real father. Those rumors, which Simpson refuted, are so notorious that Khloé even cracked a joke about them in 2016. The truth is that Kris did have an affair but not with Simpson (at least as far as we know). According toUs Weekly,the momager owned up to cheating on Simpson's attorney, Robert Kardashian, with soccer player-turned-animator Todd Waterman in her 2011 memoir "Kris Jenner ... And All Things Kardashian." On an episode of "Kocktails With Khloé,"the "Revenge Body" star admitted that her mother's cheating "destroyed" her father and remains one of Kris' biggest regrets. "I had the happiest life you could've dreamt about," Kris said during an interview on "OBJECTified" (viaUs Weekly). "But when you're in something, sometimes people think the grass is always greener, and that was, like, what I think I went through at some point." According toDaily Mail,Waterman admitted Kris was still sleeping with him when she started dating Caitlyn Jenner, meaning she may have cheated on two different people with the same guy. It's no secret that John Mayer has a reputation as a womanizer. Whether it's totally warranted or not is up for debate. The singer claimed toThe New York Timesin 2017 that he hadn't dated a lot of people "in the last five, six years." Unfortunately, his good behavior didn't erase his extensive Hollywood dating history, which is peppered with some not-so-nice moments. The singer-songwriter famously humiliated Jessica Simpson, calling her "sexual napalm" in a Playboy interview (viaUs Weekly). In the same interview, he referred to his, um, little John (yup, his penis) as a "white supremacist" because he had never been with a person of color. Despite those poorly thought-out comments, Mayer somehow found himself in the arms of Taylor Swift. His 2009 relationship with the then-19-year-old was short-lived, but her alleged breakup song will live on forever. Swift penned a scathing track titled"Dear John,"and rumors swirled that Mayer was her muse. He toldRolling Stoneat the time that he thought it was "cheap songwriting" and said he felt "humiliated." Swift claimed toGlamourthat this was "presumptuous" because she never technically said it was about him. We don't know who occupies the moral high ground on this one, but one thing is clear: Mayer still wouldn't let it go. In 2016, he tweeted (viaNME) that Swift's birthday is the "lamest day of the year." He was 39 years old at the time. And speaking of Swift... Taylor Swift might be a peach when she's in a relationship, but her exes often sing a totally different tune. The "Reputation" songstress has a notorious rep for doling out biting remarks and trashing her exes in her hit songs. According toPeople,Swift made a big deal about Joe Jonas allegedly dumping her in a 27-second phone call, but the Jonas Brother claimed on "The Ellen DeGeneres Show" at the timethat she was the one who hung up on him. Next up was Harry Styles, who reportedly received a passive aggressive shout-out during anMTVVMA acceptance speech. Then there was John Mayer, who toldRolling Stonehe was "really humiliated" by Swift's song "Dear John" and "didn't deserve it." (Honestly, what do you expect when a grown man dates a teenager?) Calvin Harris may have seen Swift's ugliest side after their 2016 split. In some now-deleted tweets (viaStereogum),the DJ accused her of trying to tear him down "for something to do." Their relationship was also subject to cheating rumors, which Swift's "Reputation" lyrics didn't do a great job of dispelling. In addition,Cosmopolitanaccused Swift of throwing actor Tom Hiddleston under the bus with "Getaway Car," which is to say nothing of the songs inspired by her splits from Jake Gyllenhaal and Joe Alwyn. Moral of the story is: If you don't want a Taylor Swift breakup song written about you, marry her. (We're looking at you, Travis Kelce.) Tristan Thompson and Khloé Kardashian began dating in 2016, just a couple of months before his ex-girlfriend, model Jordan Craig, gave birth to his first child, Prince. Unfortunately for Kardashian, her pregnancies with the NBA star would also be tainted by the presence of other women. In April 2018, multiple reports of infidelity surfaced. First,TMZspotted Thompson going to a hotel room with a mystery woman when the reality star was nine months pregnant with daughter True. The outlet then obtained video of him kissing two other women at a hookah lounge when Kardashian was three months pregnant. And it didn't end there. While Kardashian initially chose to stay with Thompson, she eventually called it quits in February 2019 after learning her man had cheated on her with Kylie Jenner's BFF, Jordyn Woods. Despite Thompson's bad rap sheet, Kardashian decided to give him yet another chance in 2020, and the pair sought to have a second child, this one via surrogate. However, before son Tatum was even born in August 2022, Thompson had cheated on her yet again, fathering a son with trainer Maralee Nichols. Thompson took to Instagram Stories to apologize directly to Kardashian, writing, "You don't deserve the heartache and humiliation I have caused you" (viaCosmopolitan). It seems that was the final straw. Asked if Kardashian would consider getting back with her ex, an insider toldUs Weeklyin 2023, "[S]he really can't imagine that ever happening." Robin Thicke met his wife, Paula Patton, in 1991 when he was just 14 years old. She was 15, and they soon became high school sweethearts, eventually tying the knot in 2005. They welcomed son Julian Fuego in 2010, and all seemed to be well until infidelity rumors emerged. In 2013, Thicke became a household name thanks to "Blurred Lines," but the song would do more harm than good. The track courted plenty of controversy with its provocative lyrics, and his infamous MTV VMAs performance with Miley Cyrus didn't help. However, it was what happened after the show that really caused the rift in his personal life. The singer was pictured grabbing 20-year-old Lana Scolaro's behind at an after-party. As she later toldLife & Style, they got handsy at the bash. "I don't think he cared what [Paula] thought," Scolaro claimed. "I was with him the whole night!" Thicke denied this but eventually admitted to being unfaithful in a 2014 deposition (viaThe Hollywood Reporter). Marvin Gaye's kids had sued the artists behind "Blurred Lines" for copyright infringement, and Thicke testified that he was too high to remember the songwriting process. Asked if he was an honest person, he addressed his February 2014 separation from Patton, saying, "No. That's why I'm separated" (viaPeople). He added, "I told my wife the truth — that's why she left me." That October, Patton made the split official and filed for divorce. Ben Affleck and Jennifer Garner married in 2005 and seemed to have a great union, but then Affleck sabotaged it,ruining his marriage. For one, he put his career first, which hurt Garner's. As she said at a promotional event in 2015, "I've been home for a long time" (viaUs Weekly). Affleck also allegedly struggled with anger issues. Not to mention that insiders claimed he had hooked up with a former nanny, Christine Ouzounian — which he denied — as well as "SNL" producer Lindsay Shookus, whom he dated publicly after his 2017 divorce. Interestingly, back in 2014, "Gone Girl" director David Fincher called Affleck's fidelity into question in the film's DVD commentary (viaNew York Daily News). "If I was his wife, I think I would be very suspicious, always, of whoever just called," he mused. Affleck and Garner initially separated in 2015, though Garner stood by his side as he entered rehab. She continued to support him after their official split, even driving him to rehab in 2018. And yet, Affleck had the audacity to tell Howard Stern in 2021 that she was to blame for his addiction. Asked what would have happened if he'd stayed married, hemade claims that had him dragged by critics. "I'd probably still be drinking," he said (viaPeople). "It's part of why I started drinking ... because I was trapped." Affleck later tried to walk back his words, saying they weren't true. Nick Cannon has had 12 kidswith six different women as of 2024, and some of the timelines, well, they overlap. In June 2021, for example, he had twins with DJ Abby De La Rosa and a son with model Alyssa Scott — just six months after having a daughter with Brittany Bell. Then, in 2022, he had five kids with five different women and, according to him, that's what his partners wanted. Speaking with"The Breakfast Club"in 2021, Cannon said he doesn't believe in monogamous relationships and claimed that becoming a father has never been his decision to make. Rather, he said it's his baby mamas who have all actively chosen to have kids with him. "Those women, and all women, are the ones that open themselves up and say, 'I would like to allow this man in my world and I will birth this child,' so it ain't my decision," he claimed. Fans were quick to clap back at that sentiment, accusing Cannon of looking for excuses for his cheating, creating broken homes, and straight-up lying. "But you married Mariah Carey, so clearly, at some point, sir, you subscribed to the institution," wrote one critic on social media (viaThe Things). Cannon himself has admitted to having been a serial cheater but toldDVSNin 2022 that he's changed and no longer hides anything from his partners because he's now involved in "consensual non-monogamy." Long before Mario Lopez found a decades-long love with wife Courtney Mazza, he had a two-week marriage to actor Ali Landry. The couple met at the 1998 Miss Teen USA pageant and dated for six years before saying "I do" in 2004. Then they annulled the whole thing just days later. Lopez eventually revealed what happened during a 2011 chat with Howard Stern. Apparently, his bachelor party got a little too rowdy, and he ended up cheating on his bride-to-be right before their wedding. As he recalled, his cousin whisked him off to Mexico where he was caught getting frisky with a woman by a pool. When Landry's sister discovered the incriminating photos, she showed them to Landry, who immediately sought an annulment. "I was wrong for obviously lying ... I shouldn't have been in that position," Lopez said (viaDaily Mail). He claimed he wasn't ready to get married but didn't find the courage to say so until after the pics surfaced. "I finally got the balls to say, 'Hey, listen, I'm not ready for this, I'm sorry,'" he recalled. Landry herself later told the"Unfolding Leadership"podcast in 2022 that the infidelity was actually much more than a one-off. "Not even a week after, I found out that it was, like, a Tiger Woods situation," she claimed. "It was truly, like, devastating." Britney Spears is convinced that Justin Timberlake cheated on her during their high-profile union, and it sounds like old habits die hard. In 2019, JT was spotted getting real cozy with "Palmer" co-star Alisha Wainwright in New Orleans. AsThe Sunreported, the singer was not wearing his wedding ring while getting handsy with Wainwright. Images and video of their night out spoke volumes, showing the pair holding hands and acting very much like they were on a date. "At one stage he grabbed her hand and rested it on his knee," a source told The Sun. The evidence was so incriminating, in fact, that Timberlake took to Instagram to apologize. "A few weeks ago I displayed a strong lapse in judgment — but let me be clear — nothing happened between me and my co-star," he wrote in a since-deleted post (viaE!). "I drank way too much that night and I regret my behavior." He went on to apologize to wife Jessica Biel and noted, "This is not the example I want to set for my son." It wasn't the first time he was accused of being unfaithful to Biel. Back in 2010, sources toldUs Weeklythat Timberlake had a three-day affair with "Perfect Couples" co-star Olivia Munn after allegedly convincing her his marriage was over. Sienna Miller has been accused of her share of indiscretions, but she was also cheated on while with Jude Law. In 2005, the couple was engaged when Law had an affair with Daisy Wright, one of his kids' nanny. Rather than denying it, Law admitted his wrongdoing. "I just want to say I am deeply ashamed and upset that I've hurt Sienna and the people most close to us," he said in a statement (viaPeople). "There is no defense for my actions, which I sincerely regret." The pair split that same month and, years later, Miller opened up about the very public scandal that rocked her world. As she toldThe Daily Beastin 2020, it was all the more difficult because she was performing in a play in London's West End at the time and had to remain professional while trying to dodge the paparazzi who were constantly chasing her there. "That was one of the most challenging moments I hope I'll ever have to experience," she admitted. "[W]ith that level of public heartbreak, to have to get out of a bed let alone stand in front of 800 people every night, it's just the last thing you want to do." The actor also revealed she's blocked out a huge chunk of that time. "There's a whole six weeks of that experience that I don't remember," she said. "I was in so much shock over it all." When Beyonce dropped "Lemonade" in 2016, she nearly broke the internet. Fans dissected every verse of every track and latched onto telling lyrics like "Becky with the good hair." It quickly became clear to anyone who listened that Jay-Z had been unfaithful in his marriage and the record was Bey's response. Jump to 2017, and the rapper admitted as much. Speaking withThe New York Times, he shared that he and Bey began making music together as a way to heal and work through their trust issues, which eventually resulted in "Lemonade" and his "4:44" album. "We were sitting in the eye of that hurricane," he mused. "And it was uncomfortable. And we had a lot of conversations." Noting how most people would have given up and chosen divorce, he said that he and his wife instead decided to tackle their pain head-on. Therapy proved a big help and taught him an important lesson: "Every emotion is connected, and it comes from somewhere." Jay said he realized he had to stop putting on a hard persona and instead embrace the vulnerability inside. "You have to survive, so you go into survival mode and ... [y]ou shut down all emotions," he explained. When that happens, it's hard to emotionally connect with your spouse, "[a]nd then all the things happen from there: infidelity." Eniko Hart was eight months pregnant in 2017 when rumors surfaced that her husband, Kevin Hart, had been unfaithful.Radarobtained photos and video of the comic getting frisky with a mystery woman inside a car outside his Miami hotel at 5 a.m., and while he denied the allegations, the evidence was pretty damning. What's more,TMZlearned shortly after that Hart was being extorted by a woman who claimed to have a sexually suggestive video of him. This time, he owned up to the headlines and apologized onInstagram. "I'm not perfect," he admitted. "I made a bad error in judgment and put myself in a bad environment where only bad things can happen and they did." Eniko ultimately chose to give her hubby another chance in order to keep her family together and ensure her unborn child had a present father. Not that it was easy. She revisited the infidelity in a 2019 episode of "Kevin Hart: Don't F*** This Up," revealing she discovered it via DM. As Eniko shared (via"Today"), someone she didn't know sent her a video of Hart with another woman. "[I]mmediately I just lost it," she recalled. "I just kept saying, 'How the f*** did you let that happen?'" But while she did forgive him, she also held him accountable to do better. "[A]s long as he behaves, we're good," she concluded. Jessica Simpson's early career was marked by her devotion to abstaining from sex before marriage, and yet, as she wrote in her 2020 memoir, "Open Book," "After I actually had sex, I understood that the emotional part was what mattered." Which is why, according to the singer, her emotional affair with her 2005 "Dukes of Hazzard" co-star Johnny Knoxville was the worst thing she could have done to then-husband Nick Lachey. "[T]o me, an emotional affair was worse than a physical one," she wrote, opening up about the deep connection she had with the equally married Knoxville. "I could share my deepest authentic thoughts with him, and he didn't roll his eyes at me," she wrote (viaPeople). "He believed in me and made me feel I could do anything." Simpson and Lachey (who began dating in 1999 when she was just 18 years old) eventually called it quits in 2005 after three years of marriage and, given her transgression, the terms of their split were rocky. "I wish we were the kind of people who could divorce and stay friends," she wrote (viaE!). "We weren't, and I regret that my actions hurt him." In a revelation that shook Hollywood, Arnold Schwarzenegger admitted in 2011 that he had fathered a son named Joseph with his family's housekeeper, Mildred Baena, back in 1997. Then, as additional details of the infidelity emerged, it became clear just how hurtful the indiscretion was to his then-wife, Maria Shriver. For one, Joseph was born just days after Shriver gave birth to their son Christopher. What's more, Baena kept working in the Schwarzenegger household, and the actor was sure Joseph's dad was Baena's husband. However, he quickly realized this wasn't the case. Even so, rather than taking ownership, he hid the secret from his wife. He succeeded for over a decade, all the while providing for Baena and their child. He even bought them a home in 2010. In the end, it was Shriver who confronted her husband about his cheating through their marriage counselor in 2011. As Schwarzenegger recalled in the 2023 Netlfix doc "Arnold" (viaThe Sun), "I thought my heart stopped. And then, I told the truth." That was all Shriver needed to know. She soon filed for divorce, ending their 25-year marriage, but as she told the"Making Space With Hoda Kotb"podcast in 2023, it took a lot for her to work through her pain. That included going to a convent where she learned the importance of giving herself the permission to be her authentic self.

title: Karlie Kloss' Husband Josh Kushner Net Worth
article_text: Karlie Kloss and Joshua Kushner are going to be parents. The couple, who just recently celebrated two years of marriage,are expectingto welcome their first child together in 2021,Peoplereports. The model has kept herrelationship with Kushnerfairly private since the pair began dating almost a decade ago. While most people are aware of Kushner's famous White House connection, Kloss's husband is still a bit of an enigma. Here's what to know aboutJoshua Kushner. Despite keeping a relatively low profile himself, Joshua's older brother, Jared, has been making a name for himself in theTrump administrationas a senior advisor. However, Joshua doesn't share Jared's political views. "It is no secret that liberal values have guided my life and that I have supported political leaders that share similar values," the 33-year-old revealed in a 2017Forbesinterview. "But neither political party has a monopoly on the truth or on constructive ideas for our country. It's important to be open minded and learn from differing opinions." Forbesalso reported that the Democrat did not vote for Trump in the 2016 election. According toThe Daily Mail, "Josh and Jared’s parents were Democratic donors until 2016." It seems as though Joshua shares his wife's political views—Kloss was vocal aboutvoting for Hillary Clinton. She regularly gets involved inpolitical campaigns, with Joshua supporting her atpolitical marchesincluding March for Our Lives in 2018. The coupletied the knoton October 18, 2018 in a small, Jewish ceremony in Upstate New York with fewer than 80 guests, according toPeople. Kloss wore a custom Dior gown. In June 2019, they had asecond, Western-themed wedding ceremony in Wyoming. Famous friends like Katy Perry, Mila Kunis, and more were in attendance. According toBustle, Kloss and Kushner first met in June 8, 2012, with the model revealing on the same date in 2016, "Four years ago today I met my best friend. I love you more everyday." Rumors about their relationship initially started when Kushner attended a Victoria's Secret Fashion Show afterparty in November 2012, withUs Weeklyreporting via a source that, "They are really cute together. [Kushner] seemed nervous and shy around everyone but handled it well. Karlie is stunning and the sweetest girl ever. She stuck close to him." Of keeping her relationship private, Kloss toldPorterin April 2018, "I know in my life what really matters to me. I'm not trying to hide that from the world; I just really like having a more private, private life. I've got nothing to hide, though!" The couple recently made a rare public appearance together at the2018 Met Gala. Forbesestimated in 2016 that the Kushners were worth $1.8 billion, with their main sources of income being real estate ($1.15 billion) and venture capital investments ($420 million). $240 million of that share comes from Oscar, a millennial-focused health insurance company Josh founded in 2012. However, CNBCreported in Marchthat the start-up is now valued at $3.2 billion. According toCelebrity Net Worth, Josh Kushner's net worth is $800 million, although the accuracy of that exact figure is unclear. Kloss's new husband alsoco-foundedinvestment firm Thrive Capital, which hasties to Instagram. He's also agraduateof Harvard Business School. Of his business ventures, Kushner toldAriana Huffingtonin 2015, "It's incredibly difficult to build a business... I think it's important to kind of ignore when people say good things about you especially in this industry... Just be incredibly focused." A source revealed toPeoplethat in June 2018, Kloss converted to Judaism, a step whichIvanka Trumpalso took before marrying Jared. Way back in March 2013, Kloss toldPeoplethat she was ecstatic that Kushner wasn't a part of the fashion world. She described her then-boyfriend as, “sonot in fashion. It’s really refreshing to leave all the fashion shows and shoots and chaos totally behind.” From the start of their relationship, it sounds like Kloss has been enjoying the quiet life with her new beau. Kushnerproposedin the summer of 2018 in upstate New York. As insider toldPeople, "They’re both overjoyed and happily celebrating. Their hearts are full and they’re excited to build their future together." Both Karlie and Joshua revealed the news on their respective Instagram accounts in July 2018. Karliewrote, "I love you more than I have words to express. Josh, you’re my best friend and my soulmate. I can’t wait for forever together. Yes a million times over 💍," while Joshua simply captionedhis photo, "fiancée ❤️." Karlie also sharedphotos of the ringon her Instagram Stories.

title: Gigi Hadid and Kendall Jenner earn millions — but most models make less than $50,000 a year
article_text: New York Fashion Weekhas descended on the city once again. As designers showcase fashion collections worth thousands of dollars, runway models bring the shows to life. But behind the scenes, the financial situation of many models who walk in New York Fashion Week isn't as glamorous as it seems. Models who manage to become household names command high rates for their work. The 10 highest-paid models made a collective $109.5 million between June 2016 and June 2017,according to Forbes. The top spot on the most recent list went to 22-year-old Kendall Jenner, who earned a total of $22 million. That's more than double the $10 million Jenner, who has over 85 million Instagram followers, made the year before. Gisele Bündchen, 37, was the second-highest paid model with $17.5 million in earnings. She came in first on the2016 Forbes list, with $30.5 million. For the rest of the industry, which the Council of Fashion Designers of America has said is "in transition," thefinancial story is much different. While many models have closets filled with expensive clothes — often received aspayment for their work— most do not have bank accounts to match. In New York,models earn $48,130 on average, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. That's only a third of theaverage annual Manhattanite salaryof $144,716. "Models—many of whom are minors—have low bargaining power and are frequently not paid all of their earned wages, are paid wages late, are paid only after complaining about non-payment, are paid in 'trade' instead of money, or are simply not paid at all," former model and founder and executive director of theModels Alliance, Sara Ziff,told The Daily Beast's Miranda Frum. Kelly Mittendorf, 23, who retired from modeling in 2015 after spending five years in the industry, recentlyspoke to the New York Timesabout her experience. Here's Mittendorf: "I never made good money as a model. I went into debt with every single one of my agencies at one point or another. An agency has for each girl an account, and if they need to have the girl come from Arizona to New York in order to build her portfolio, the agency will front the expenses for her plane ticket, for paying the photographers, for printing the photos, for the physical portfolio itself, for the comp cards that need to be developed, for the retouching, for new clothes to go on castings with, for a model apartment for her to stay in." While there's no guarantee that a model's career earnings will justify the upfront costs, one way or another she is required to repay the agency. In Mittendorf's case, that amounted to five figures of debt. "I was lucky to kind of be able to climb out of that,"she told the New York Times. "It took years."

title: 'Scandal' To End After Season 7
article_text: ByMadeline Berg, Former Staff. Shonda Rhimes'Scandalwill come to an end next year, according toa report from TVLine. The series, which is part of ABC's popular T.G.I.T Thursday night lineup, has been a hit for the network and has helped secure Rhimes' dominance and make a big name out of star Kerry Washington, who plays Washington D.C.'s "fixer" Olivia Pope. This should not come as a huge surprise to big Shondaland fans, as Rhimes herself said that the show would have a shorter shelf life than her original hit,Grey's Anatomy,which is now in its 13th season."I feel like there is a finite amount of Scandal to be told," shetold NPR in 2013. "So I know what the end of Scandal will be, and I feel really good about that. And I can see where the end point is." Thus the show's conclusion was the decision of Rhimes, not the network.Among the advertiser-coveted 18 to 49 demographic, the show was among the 20 highest-rated shows of 2016.The current season averages 5.699 million viewers and 1.46 viewers in the 18-49 demo. While this marks a drop from the fifth season's average of 7.18 million viewers, the current live number is impressive considering the steady decline of live-viewership.Scandalremains one of ABC's most popular series and a large reason why the network routinely beats the other broadcasters on Thursday nights. These ratings, of course, have allowed the network to pull in a hefty amount in ad revenue. At its peak,Scandalwas part of a Thursday night block that brought ABC over half a billion dollars. In 2016,Scandalbrought in $75 million for ABC--more thanHow to Get Away with MurderorThe Catch,according to iSpot.tv. "What Shonda Rhimes possesses is this extraordinary instinct and compass for what our audience needs," then-president of ABC Entertainment group Paul Leetold FORBESin 2013."That Shonda is free and has a huge amount of power to pursue her vision is precisely how the magic happens." The network isn't the only beneficiary ofScandal's popularity. The show's stars have risen to prominence--and their wallets have grown--with the series. Washington routinely lands high on Forbes' list ofhighest-paid TV actresses.Last year, she pulled in $12 million, with about half of that coming from her salary from the show. Being on the show has made her well-known enough to land lucrative endorsement deals with the likes of Neutrogena and a commercial with Apple Music. As a black lead on a broadcast series, Washington's star turn has also brought much-needed diversity to prime time. After the success ofScandal, Rhimes brought another African American woman--Viola Davis,the first black woman to ever win the Emmy for Best Lead Actress in a Drama--to the limelight onHow to Get Away with Murder.On broadcast TV, only 22.6% of series regulars are of underrepresented racial minorities according to the 2016Annenberg report on diversity. In dramas, likeScandal,this percentage drops. Unfortunately, that means two dramas with black leads is a big deal for the industry. “There’s always room for our film and television, for our art, to be more representative of who we are as a culture. I think for me especially, being a person of color and a woman, you really see that intersection,"she toldWWD.

title: Haylie Duff Net Worth
article_text: Haylie Duff is an American actress, TV presenter, film producer, and businesswoman who has a net worth of $5 million. Haylie Duff is the older sister of fellow actressHilary Duff. Haylie's dance work led to guest starring roles on multiple shows and television films, including "Hope," "The Amanda Show," "Chicago Hope," "Lizzie McGuire," "Boston Public," "Third Watch," "American Dreams," "That's So Raven," "One on One," and "Joan of Arcadia." She co-starred on the hit series, "7th Heaven" for two seasons and has since appeared in such projects as "Backwoods," "Love Takes Wing," "Love Finds a Home," "My Nanny's Secret," "Fear Island," "Home Invasion," and "A Holiday Engagement." Duff has also appeared in the films "Napoleon Dynamite," "Dishdogz," "My Sexiest Year," and "Tug," and she provided the voice of Summer Wheatly on the short-lived animated series version of "Napoleon Dynamite." Haylie Duff was born Haylie Katherine Duff on February 19, 1985, in Houston, Texas. She began studying ballet when she was a child and started performing with the Houston Metropolitan Dance Company when she was ten. She is the older sister of actress Hilary Duff. The Duff gals' mother, Susan Colleen, is a film producer who has produced titles like "The Perfect Man" and "Material Girls." She also co-executive produced "A Cinderella Story." Susan was previously a homemaker before she became a producer and the manager of daughter Hilary. Duff's father, Robert Erhard Duff, is a partner and owner of a chain of convenience stores. (Photo by Paul Archuleta/Getty Images) Duff began her acting career with a series of guest appearances in made-for-TV movies like "True Women." She also guest-starred on TV shows that were popular at the time, such as "The Amanda Show," "Chicago Hope," "Boston Public," and "Third Watch." Haylie became known in late 2002 when she began appearing in the show her sister starred in, "Lizza McGuire." Duff played Amy Sanders. Two years later, she made a guest appearance on "That's So Raven," appearing as Katina Jones. Duff nabbed her first feature film role when she was cast as Summer Wheatley in "Napoleon Dynamite," a role for which she received her first Teen Choice Award. In 2005, she was cast in the popular WB TV show "7th Heaven" as Sandy Jameson. Haylie joined the Broadway cast of "Hairspray" as Amber Von Tussle in June 2006 but left the role in October 2006. She starred in 2006's "Material Girls" with her sister, Hilary, and she is also listed as a co-producer on the film. Other straight-to-DVD films Duff worked on include "Love Finds a Home," "My Nanny's Secret," "My Sexiest Year," and "Backwoods." Duff appeared in "Tug," "Fear Island," "Foodfight," and "Slightly Single in L.A." between 2008 and 2015. She also hosted the reality TV show "Legally Blonde: The Musical — The Search for Elle Woods." Ilya S. Savenok/Getty Images Duff is also an accomplished singer and has recorded several singles for soundtracks for "In Search of Santa," "The Lizzie McGuire Movie," "Material Girls," and "A Cinderella Story" with her sister. Many of them appear on the "Disneymania" discs. In 2008, she recorded background vocals for the track "On the Rise Again" fromKool G Rap'salbum "Half a Klip." Haylie sang "A Whatever Life" for the soundtrack of "Stuck in the Suburbs." She also recorded "Sweetest Pain" for the "Raising Helen" soundtrack. Duff sang a duet called "Babysitting is a Bum Deal" withSeth MacFarlaneas his "Family Guy" character Stewie on the album "Family Guy: Live in Las Vegas." She also is credited as a writer and co-writer on several songs for Hilary's first two studio albums. On Hilary's song "Sparks" from her album "Breathe in. Breathe Out.," Haylie contributed a whistling part. She began a blog in 2012 that she called "Real Girl's Kitchen." It was later picked up and made into a TV show by the Cooking Channel in 2014. Duff released her first book "The Real Girl's Kitchen" in 2013. She started her own children's fashion line called Little Moon Society in 2017. Haylie has been linked to Matt Rosenberg since 2012. The two announced their engagement in 2014. They have two children together, Ryan Ava and Lulu Gray. In February 2015, Haylie paid $1.3 million for a home in Studio City, California. She sold this home in December 2016 for $1.855 million. In October 2016, she paid $2.7 million for a home in Studio City, California. The seller wasAshley Tisdale. Haylie listed this home for $3.195 million in March 2021, ultimately selling it for right around her asking price. In November 2020, Duff paid $1.95 million for a home in Austin, Texas. She listed this home for sale in January 2024 for $3.25 million.

title: A Real Housewife who's back on the show after leaving 4 years ago says she was shocked by how nasty the cast feuds had gotten
article_text: Lydia McLaughlin says that the time was right for her to return to Bravo's "The Real Housewives of Orange County." "It was actually really hard to decide to leave," McLaughlin told INSIDER ofquitting the showafter just one season in 2013. "I think a lot of people thought I was crazy. One of the producers actually said, 'It’s lightning in a bottle and it doesn’t happen twice,' because I told them maybe I’ll just take a break.I just felt like my kids were really young and I wanted to have another kid close in age to them. And so it was the right decision for my family, but it was hard." Four years later, McLaughlin and her husband, Doug, have added on to her family with a third son and they've created a new high-end men's magazine called "Nobleman."With that, McLaughlindecided to end her break and continue her story on the 12th season of Bravo's longest-running "Real Housewives" show. "I think that’s a really interesting kind of story to follow, the two of us really going out, and taking a risk, and starting a magazine, working together, just the two of us to fulfill our dreams," the 36-year-old said. "And then obviously having the new baby being two years old, I felt like he was old enough where he literally isn’t attached to me nursing anymore, so I can be more involved and kind of have something on my own," she continued. "Those six months of taping 'Real Housewives' were great, it was much better even than last time." After the first time around, McLaughlin said she learned some important lessons about trust that she brought with her to this season. "Last time, I was really nervous about editing or sharing something, for example, my faith is really important to me and sacred in my life, and I was nervous a lot times when I was filming and talking about that," she said. "I was scared about the way it would be portrayed or how it might be edited. And this time around, I was just more free with it. I think if you do a reality show, you really have to trust the production and trust that your story will get told." Take a smarter break in your day - and see how far you get. Although she was more prepared for the rigors of production, McLaughlin was somewhat blindsided by the level of feuding between her cast mates. She hasn't caught up on the show after she left – referring to seeing what was happening on the show and with her cast mates without her as "bittersweet," so she didn't have an accurate idea of where the women's relationships stood. "I hadn’t watched it, so I was assuming that they don’t like each other right now, but they just need to talk and it’ll be fine," the self-titled "Friendship Whisperer" told us. "And then I quickly realized it’s not something that talking is necessarily going to help, it might make it worse. These ladies have really hurt each other and there’s a lot of pain there, so maybe they’re not ready to move on. You know, a cup of coffee and a lunch date isn’t going to help. So I kind of had to reevaluate my plan and try to figure out what the best thing is for everybody." "The Real Housewives of Orange County" returns Monday at 9 p.m. on Bravo.

title: Ed Sheeran thinks that people would've liked his 'Game of Thrones' cameo more if he was killed on the episode
article_text: Ed Sheeran thinks his "Game of Thrones" character is still somewhere in Westeros but shouldn't be. The 27-year-old musician spoke with BuzzFeed andtalked about his controversial cameo on the hit HBO show's seventh seasonand said he thinks his character should have met his end. title: Maria Shriver Net Worth
article_text: Maria Shriver is an American journalist, author, and former First Lady of California who has a net worth of $200 million. Maria Shriver is a member of the Kennedy family through her mother, Eunice Kennedy Shriver. Eunice was one of nine children born to Joseph andRose Kennedy. Eunice's siblings included PresidentJohn F. Kennedy,Robert F. Kennedy, andTed Kennedy. Maria began her journalism career at KYW-TV in Philadelphia before joining CBS News and later NBC News, where she became a co-anchor for "CBS Morning News" and "Sunday Today." At NBC, she reported for "Dateline" and anchored numerous specials, winning multiple Emmy and Peabody awards. She served as California's First Lady from 2003-2011 while married toArnold Schwarzenegger, focusing on women's empowerment and Alzheimer's advocacy through initiatives like The Women's Conference. As an author, she's written several bestselling books, including "Ten Things I Wish I'd Known Before I Went Out Into The Real World" and "I've Been Thinking." She launched The Sunday Paper, a digital newsletter, and continues her journalism work through NBC News as a special anchor covering women's issues and social topics. Maria Shriver and Arnold Schwarzenegger have four children, includingKatherine Schwarzenegger(born 1989) – Author and lifestyle blogger, married to actorChris Pratt, Christina Schwarzenegger (born 1991) – Producer and filmmaker;Patrick Schwarzenegger(born 1993) – Actor and model, Christopher Schwarzenegger (born 1997) – The youngest, graduated from the University of Michigan. (Photo by Pool BENAINOUS/CATARINA/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images) Maria Owings Shriver was born on November 6, 1955, in Chicago, Illinois. Her father was a well-known politician named Sargent Shriver, and her mother was Eunice Kennedy Shriver, an activist and member of the affluent and influential Kennedy family. Because of her family roots, Maria was essentially born into royalty – or as close as one can get to royalty in the United States. While growing up, Shriver watched her uncle John. F. Kennedy win an election to become the President of the United States. Two years later, she watched her uncle get assassinated. Maria Shriver is the daughter of Eunice Kennedy Shriver (sister of President John F. Kennedy) and Sargent Shriver. This makes her JFK's niece. Her maternal aunts and uncles included: Her first cousins include: Her maternal grandparents were Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. and Rose Fitzgerald Kennedy, who established the Kennedy political dynasty. Through this lineage, she is also related to current political figures like Joe Kennedy III (her first cousin once removed) and other members of the extended Kennedy family. Raised in a Roman Catholic household, Maria attended high school in Maryland. After graduating, she enrolled at Manhattanville College before transferring to Georgetown University and earning her Bachelor of Arts degree in American Studies. Shriver first became passionate about journalism during her father's vice-presidential campaign in 1972. After graduating from college, she worked with CBS and eventually became co-anchor of "The CBS Morning News." After switching to NBC, she co-anchored "Sunday Today" until the end of the '80s. She then anchored shows like "NBC Nightly News" and "Dateline NBC." She returned to journalism after becoming the First Lady of California, although she eventually stepped away because of a potential conflict of interest. Maria then became completely disillusioned with American media after the death ofAnna Nicole Smith, vowing never to return to this industry. However, she joined NBC once again in 2013, working as a special anchor who focuses on women's issues in America. She also fills in as a substitute anchor on "Today" from time to time. Outside of journalism, Shriver has appeared in a number of movies, including "Last Action Hero," and television series such as "That's So Raven." She also served as the executive producer for the four-part HBO documentary "The Alzheimer's Project." In addition, Maria is known for authoring several books, including "I've Been Thinking…: Reflections Prayers and Meditations for a Meaningful Life," which became a bestseller. Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images Because Maria Shriver is a direct descendant of the famed Kennedy family, she receives considerable income through inheritance and other assets/trusts set up in the family name. The Kennedys are essentially considered a royal lineage in the United States, and Shriver certainly benefits from her connection to the family in a financial sense. Documents show that Shriver collects income from assets that include "Vornado Realty Trust" and "Vornado Realty Inc." Each of these assets is valued at $7.5 million. Reports suggest that the Kennedys have collected more than $170 million since 1998 – and that's just in dividends. The family's financial assets are set up in an ingenious manner – using a system that accepts partnership units instead of cash in order to defer capital gains taxes and depreciation. Maria Shriver met Arnold Schwarzenegger in 1977 when they were introduced at a charity tennis tournament. The pair eventually married in 1986 and subsequently had four children together, all of whom were born in Los Angeles. Their daughter Katherine is married to actor Chris Pratt. In 2011, Shriver and Schwarzenegger announced that they were getting separated, and Maria quickly moved out of the family home. Later, the reason for their split was apparently revealed when Arnold Schwarzenegger publicly admitted that he had fathered another child out of wedlock with the family maid, Mildred Patricia Baena. Shriver had previously confronted her husband about the affair after she became suspicious. Arnold's extramarital child was born 14 years prior to him making the announcement – well before he entered politics. He and Shriver eventually finalized their divorce in 2017. In 2013, Shriver started dating Matthew Dowd, a political consultant and strategist who had previously worked on Schwarzenegger's reelection campaign. According to various sources, Maria Shriver was set to receive up to $200 million after her divorce from Arnold Schwarzenegger. This is because of Arnold's high net worth, which was at least double the amount Shriver received at the time of their divorce. In terms of their children, the split was handled amicably with shared custody of their two underage kids. Maria Shriver has been quite active in the real estate market, particularly after splitting from Arnold Schwarzenegger. In 2002, Arnold and Maria paid $4.8 million for a 6-acre property in LA's Brentwood neighborhood. The property features a 14,500-square-foot home with a tennis court, pool, and never-ending ocean views. Arnold continued owning and occupying this home after their split. After the divorce was finalized, Shriver paid $10 million for an 11,000-square-foot home in Brentwood, not far from the family home she once shared with her husband. In June 2022, Maria paid $12.2 million for a property immediately next door. In 2017, Shriver reportedly started shopping for homes with the intention of giving them to her two children who had just graduated from university. title: The 3 Biggest Mistakes 'The Walking Dead' Made In The Season 9 Premiere
article_text: ByErik Kain, Senior Contributor. AMC's zombie drama returned last Sunday with the season 9 premiere---an episode which marked an uptick in overall quality forThe Walking Dead,but still made some old, avoidable foibles that almost look like bad habits at this point. New showrunner Angela Kang has been a writer on the show since Season 2, and it appears that even with improved dialogue and cinematography, she's been unable to shed some of the show's most annoying proclivities. Old habits die hard, it seems. But,like Gregory and a few other characters, they really do need to die. Let's take a look at three big mistakes the show made in its Season 9 premiere, and how each could have been easily avoided with a little more quality control and a little bit more courage. With some very small changes, this could have been a much better episode. Spoilers through Season 9 of 'The Walking Dead' follow. 1. The museum scene. Things got off to something of a bad start when our heroes went to D.C. I'm going to list this as a two-part problem. My first problem with this sequence is a creative disagreement with the show's producers and writers. My second is pretty much just the objective truth. First: An excursion to Washington D.C. to find seeds and other tools should have been a much more interesting, extended story. I think you could easily fit in an episode or two with a small group of scavengers going to D.C. and getting into various pickles there. That it was just one not very good scene at a museum really diminished something I was looking forward to, stripping of it of almost all its potential as an interesting little adventure (which the show has so few of these days.) Second: The museum scene was just bad. There was very little explanation as to why they needed all these heavy objects---surely there were more modern versions of things like carts and ploughs which they could find on farms or in hardware stores. Worse, the entire sequence with the glass floor was embarrassingly bad. The floor itself would not have cracked so easily. That kind of glass is made to withstand a great deal more impact. But even if they'd had it broken to begin with, making it more precarious from the get-go, there was no reason they couldn't have found another way around it. Passing items over the railing would have worked. Ezekiel could have avoided walking the entire length of the breaking glass by simply turning to one side or the other once exiting the stairs. This is a classic example ofThe Walking Dead'swriters treating its viewers with contempt. We aren't that stupid. And neither are these characters. These hardened survivors of the apocalypse should know better---and would know better if they weren't continually written into these same corners over and over and over again. This entire sequence was insulting to our intelligence and had no business being in a premiere cable TV show. 2. The death scene. The second big problem of the night came shortly after the first. Our group, comprised largely of characters we know and then also one other guy named Ken, is bringing the museum loot back to Alexandria and Hilltop when a small mob of zombies shuffles up behind them. This leads to much fear and commotion, despite this being a much smaller zombie mob than we've seen the same survivors deal with easily in the past. One thing leads to another and they decide to all run away and, bafflingly, abandon the horses. In an apocalypse where cars are no longer an option, horses must be one of the most prized---and hard to come by---resources out there. But a few zombies can scare Rick and his band of hardened survivors away regardless. Utterly unconvincing. So when Ken (I think that was his name) runs back to save the horses we know right away he's going to die. For reasons the show cannot provide, a zombie manages to sneak up on him and nobody can get to him in time to save him. Maybe that looked okay on paper, but it didn't work on TV and left us with that bad, unconvincing taste in our mouths. The Fix: Now, you can fix #1 and #2 in one fell swoop pretty easily (but it won't fix #3.) Simply have the glass in the museum already breaking when they get there. Have them do everything in their power to avoid standing on it (like actual people with a self-preservation motive would do) but have something go wrong. Maybe there's one last item (like the cart) that they can't get around the glass and they lose control and instead of Ezekiel falling through the glass, Ken falls through the glass and is torn apart by zombies in the most gruesome manner possible. Now we can avoid the bad parts of the museum scene and cut the other scene entirelyandwe get a more shocking, gory death. Everybody wins! There's just one problem . . . . 3. Using a character we don't know as a catalyst for an important event. Don't do that. Every single significant death in a show needs to have a reason or serve some higher purpose, even if it just to shock audiences. Ken's death in the Season 9 premiere served a purpose, but it didn't connect with us emotionally. It was a catalyst for Gregory's final, fatal betrayal of Maggie. It led him to make a very stupid power play, the straw that broke the Maggie's back, as it were, when he got the blacksmith drunk and convinced him to kill Maggie. The problem? There's no payoff. No emotional weight. Because Ken was not an established character at all. He was introduced just to die. His parents were introduced just so that the father could become Gregory's tool in his latest horrible scheme. This is something we saw happen from time to time inLost.Characters were suddenly introduced on the island (how did they get there?) only to be killed off later that episode. We, as viewers, never gave a damn because we had no connection to these strangers. This is hardly the first timeThe Walking Deadhas done this, of course. That scene where Simon stops Maggie's caravan and kills that one guy---Dave was it?---who we only just met moments earlier. Another scene I think all the way back in Season 5 where a brand new character and love interest of Beth's falls into a zombie-infested cellar. I'm pretty sure that happened but I don't remember it well or care at all because we never care about brand new characters. Okay, that's not always true. A skilled filmmaker can make us care deeply about characters we just met. Think of the opening moments ofA Quiet Place,or the puppy scene inJohn Wick.But that takes a bit of work. You have to establish an emotional connection in a very short period of time to a character (or dog) we just met. It can be done, but it takes more than a twenty second conversation on the road followed by a swift death and a bunch of melodramatic "blame Maggie" scenes. (Seriously you miserable pricks, I get that your son just died and that sucks and you should feel sad, but blaming Maggie for this is absurd. It's the zombie apocalypse. People are dying all the time. Grow up.) The Fix: So how could you fix this problem and #1 and #2? Given that the blacksmith's family was not introduced in prior seasons, the only way I can figure it out is to make the D.C. trip longer. Three or four episodes at least. Have Ken play a much larger role and get us to really like him. Introduce his parents early on, too. Let us get to know them at least a little before he is ripped to tiny giblets by the walking dead. Establishing Ken as an important, likable character before offing him would definitely help, especially if it was a surprise. I add "likable" to the mix because, as we saw in season 4 ofFear The Walking Dead,introducing a character everyone hates and then making him the final "big death" of the season is also terrible writing. So those are my big three problems with the Season 9 premiere. Without them, I think it would have been a really strong episode. With them, because they're so easily avoidable and so in keeping with allThe Walking Dead'sworst habits over the years, the episode was just okay. It had some very good moments, but those were sullied by these inexplicably bad ones. So this is my message---my plea---my best advice to Angela Kang: Every episode needs to be checked over and checked again for this kind of mistake. Quality Control's job needs to be finding every instance of aWalking Deadcharacter making an out-of-character decision or acting stupid for no reason (other than to further the plot) and ensure that it's rewritten to make sense. Sure, some people who watch this show are not particularly discerning, who think just because the premise is outlandish nothing needs to be plausible, but a great deal of the audience (the dwindling audience, I might add) wants this show to be a realistic take on the apocalypse. Make these actions add up.Earn your outcomes. Fortunately,I think the next two episodes are less impacted by this all-too-familiarWalking Deadnonsense, though I can't speak to the rest of the season. Let me know what you think of all thison TwitterorFacebook. Cheers! Bonus:When Rick walks into the Sanctuary a bunch of people kind of turn in awe and one of the Saviors says "That's Rick Grimes. He ended the war!" and it's just such a classicWalking Deadmoment where anyone with half a brain watching just slaps their forehead and shakes their head in pure wonder and amazement that anyone would write a line so on-the-nose and that, once filmed, it would ever manage to make the final cut.Not only does nobody actually talk like that, it's just totally superfluous. We know Rick ended the war. He also started it. We don't need some weird recap from some random side character. Thanks a lot, Captain Obvious. Here's my video review:
